canonicalization.inputSemanticHash: lowercase SHA-256 of UTF-8 JSON.stringify over the parsed normative input with object key and array order preserved and no appended LF; acceptance requirements and risks omit only item state/evidence, while capture omits top-level state and normalizes runtimeImageDigest.value, fonts.resolvedFiles and scenarioEvidence to null; every other input uses the complete parsed value
canonicalization.tupleId: FFVT- + lowercase SHA-256 of JSON.stringify(canonical tuple)
canonicalization.streamHash: lowercase SHA-256 of each canonical JSON tuple followed by one LF, in declared generator order
canonicalization.tupleIdStreamHash: lowercase SHA-256 of each tuple ID followed by one LF, in the same order
canonicalization.requirementGeneratorOrder: acceptance.json requirements source order; no lexical re-sort
subjectTupleRules: Visit subjectGeneratorOrder; inside each family visit the referenced routeSubjectSet or localSubjects array in its declared order.
Every subject tuple uses the referenced axisSuite.defaultRow expanded through axisCatalogs.viewportZoomProfiles.
A route subject sets routeId to that route; a capability or action subject resolves routeId from production-inventory.json and sets null for a global subject.
Component, component-case, surface, surface-target and risk subjects use the first routeId of the referenced routeSubjectSet as their route anchor.
Exactly the named subject field is populated; every other nullable subject field is null.
axisTupleRules: Regenerate axis rows with pairClosureAlgorithm and the referenced axisSuite axisOrder/values.
Visit regenerated rows in pair-closure encounter order.
Every axis tuple has family axis-pair-closure, subjectType route and routeId equal to the first routeId of the referenced routeSubjectSet; every other nullable subject field is null.
responsiveTupleRules: Visit routes.json routes in source order; inside each route visit widths 320, 390, 430, 768, 1024, 1280, 1440 and 1920 in that order.
Resolve height from the matching z100 axisCatalog viewport profile; zoomPercent is 100.
Fixed axes are role owner-admin, input fine-pointer, state populated, density comfortable, motion no-preference, contrastMode normal and tenantBrand the requirement's first declared theme.
subjectType is route, routeId is the visited route and every other nullable subject field is null.
pairClosureAlgorithm: Start with the first value of every axis in axisOrder.
Visit every unordered axis-index pair left-to-right where leftIndex < rightIndex.
For each pair visit the left values, then right values, in declared order.
Copy the default row, replace the two visited values, and append only if its canonical JSON has not appeared.
Pair-row IDs are FFVA- plus lowercase SHA-256 of that canonical row JSON.
canonicalization.fullCartesianAlgorithm: Depth-first recursion in axisOrder; values are visited in declared order; the last axis changes fastest.
sharedMatrixTupleRules: Visit sharedMatrixGeneratorOrder, then use fullCartesianAlgorithm with each matrix axisOrder and axisValues.
Resolve subjectBinding through that matrix's subjectBindings object into surfaceTargetId and routeId.
Every shared tuple has family shared-full-cartesian, requirementId null, matrixId equal to the matrix id, subjectType surface-target and every other nullable subject field null.
canonicalization.selectorAlgorithm: * selects every routes.json row in source order; a terminal * selects source-order route strings with that literal prefix; otherwise exact route equality; results are de-duplicated in source order.

verificationPlanRootSerialization.rule: Initialize SHA-256. For every requirementBinding in requirementGeneratorOrder, construct a new object with requirementLineFieldOrder insertion order and append JSON.stringify(object) plus LF. Then, for every shared matrix in sharedMatrixGeneratorOrder, construct a new object with sharedMatrixLineFieldOrder insertion order and append JSON.stringify(object) plus LF. The lowercase hex digest is verificationPlanRootSha256. No BOM, whitespace, trailing spaces or additional line is included.

sharedFullCartesianMatrices.purpose: Full Cartesian whitelabel proof for tenant, customer and personnel authentication/onboarding surfaces.
Full Cartesian whitelabel proof for every e-mail and PDF/export evidence target.
Full Cartesian A to B to A switch proof without stale paint, cache leakage or identity leakage.

routeParity.rule: The FFC-ROUTE-001 subject-coverage family contains one tuple for every route, capability and action; globals use routeId null and may not be silently assigned to one route.

responsive.rule: The responsive-route-width-full family is the exact routes.json source order crossed with the eight width order; it is never pairwise-sampled.

whitelabel.rule: Each named matrix is a full Cartesian product over every declared applicable axis and must be proven in addition to each linked requirement's own tuple stream.

rules: The evidence report matrix SHA-256 and verificationPlanRootSha256 equal this root-bound manifest exactly.
Every requirement tuple and every linked shared-matrix tuple is executed exactly once; unknown, duplicate, missing, sampled, manual, skipped and NOT_RUN tuples fail closed.
Shard ordinal ranges are contiguous, non-overlapping, begin at zero and end at tupleCount; concatenated shard ID/payload streams reproduce the declared hashes.
The verifier recomputes every tuple ID from canonicalTuple and recomputes all stream hashes; a caller-supplied ID or count is never trusted.
Each assertion binds the exact role, input, state, viewport width/height, zoom, density, motion, contrast, tenant-brand and subject IDs present in canonicalTuple.
An assertion without at least one machine assertionId and one content-addressed attachmentId cannot pass.
Shared Cartesian matrix evidence is reusable only for its exact requirementIds and exact implementation HEAD.
